//: Age a live campaign: run the geoscape clock fast for a fixed span of REAL time, then put the clock back exactly as it was found.
//lever: GeoLevelController.Timing (GeoLevelController.cs:229) -> Base.Core.Timing.Scale (:79) and .Paused (:100). The console command `geo_speed` is the same lever with a x300 multiplier baked in (GeoLevelController.cs:1683); setting Scale directly is the same thing without the multiplier to guess at.
//real: This is REAL simulation, not a calendar cosmetic. The hourly callback (GeoLevelController.cs:761) runs research, faction income, bases and manufacturing (:777-833), and at midnight the building/diplomacy/alien/mission daily pipeline (:779-781, :836-868).
//rate: MEASURED: Scale 3600 unpaused for 28 real seconds advanced the campaign by 1 day 00:02:09.6. Budget about one in-game day per 28 real seconds.
//ceiling: 3600 IS THE CEILING THIS PROJECT HAS PROVED. Higher is not automatically faster-and-safe: the scheduler reads Timing.Now ONCE per pass and dequeues whatever is overdue (TimingScheduler.cs:425-441), and the hourly callback schedules its successor from the clock it woke up on (:833) - so a frame that jumps over several hours COLLAPSES them into one callback and can miss midnight entirely. Keep advancement under one in-game hour per rendered frame. A `geo_speed 30` (Scale 9000) trial lost its endpoint and is not evidence either way.
//restore: The finally block restores BOTH Scale and Paused to whatever they were, so an aged campaign is handed back paused if it was found paused. Ageing is expensive; snapshot the result (`connect snapshot`) rather than paying for it twice.

steps.//: Read BEFORE anything is written - these two values are the whole contract of the finally block.
TimeUnit is a struct with one private TimeSpan (TimeUnit.cs:16), so it projects as a handle; its ToString is the round-trippable d.hh:mm:ss.
The only wait with no predicate. Game time is driven by real time through Scale, so 'run for this long' IS the fast-forward, and it is a SUCCESS when it elapses.
Stop the clock BEFORE reading, or the two readings below straddle a moving target.

finally.//: MANDATORY. A plan that left Scale at 3600 hands a human a campaign running 3600x, which reads as the game having broken itself.
